messages:
Mike R.: Heads-up — nightly small-decode jobs show a weird latency spike on flash-paged variants, only for short sequences (<= 16). hoping @everyone saw the perf alert :eyes:
Sara K.: saw it in the dashboard, looks like spikes align with kernel selector churn around batch boundaries
Josh L.: any raw profiles? could be KV cache fragmentation + continuous-batching interact weirdly
Mike R.: attaching clipped profiler output (small excerpt):
```
# bench-runner --suite=decode-small --kernel=auto --kvcache=on --warm=30
[00:00:12] batch=1 kernel=flash_paged ms/token=3.4 kv_hit_rate=0.92
[00:00:13] batch=1 kernel=fused_attn ms/token=4.1 kv_hit_rate=0.88
[00:00:14] batch=2 kernel=flash_paged ms/token=3.6 kv_hit_rate=0.40  <-- drop
[00:00:15] batch=3 kernel=fused_attn ms/token=5.0 kv_hit_rate=0.35
# selector toggled flash_paged <-> fused_attn 4x in 8s
```
Tanya P.: interesting — kv_hit_rate dropping that fast smells like KV cache eviction or addressing mismatch when continuous batching merges inflight streams
Josh L.: could be "switchback" where prefill chooses one kernel then decode path picks another because of transient seq-len/batch-size distribution. triggers bad kernel-launch costs repeatedly
Mike R.: exactly. i coined it "switchback" in my head. hypothesis: selector uses instant metrics (current batch shapes + recent latency) without smoothing, so a single low-hit mini-batch flips decision and we pay kernel-launch + cache re-layout repeatedly
Sara K.: do we have hysteresis/rolling averages in the selector? last I checked it used exponential moving average but maybe with too short a window
Tanya P.: selector config excerpt: `kernel_selector.window_ms=1000`, `decay=0.8`, `min_samples=3` — may be too aggressive for high churn workloads
Josh L.: quick reproducer: run `./tools/mini_workload --pattern=short_then_varied --runs=500` and hook `KVCACHE_STATS` env. on my laptop I see periodic kv_hit_rate dips when minibatches align wrong
Mike R.: local run snippet (trimmed):
```
run 112: kernel=flash_paged ms/token=3.5 kv_hit_rate=0.91
run 113: kernel=fused_attn ms/token=5.2 kv_hit_rate=0.33  # cold-page fills
run 114: kernel=flash_paged ms/token=3.7 kv_hit_rate=0.89
```
Sara K.: that explains the 2x latency wobble. also noticed p99 tails go up 20-30% during switchbacks
Tanya P.: two proposed fixes: 1) add selector hysteresis: require >X% benefit sustained for Y ms before switching; 2) improve KV cache addressing to avoid evicting warmed prefixes on small merges
Josh L.: +1 for hysteresis. low-risk and measurable. we should also expose a metric `selector_switch_rate` to trace correlated spikes
Mike R.: can we try `window_ms=5000` and `min_samples=10` in CI bench to see impact? i'll run a canary tonight
Sara K.: i'll add `selector_switch_rate`, `windowed_kv_hit_rate` and `kernel_launch_count` to the console charts so we can correlate with customer traffic patterns
Josh L.: also want to test forcing `kernel=flash_paged` and `kvcache=off` to isolate whether KV behavior is primary cause
Tanya P.: ordering: Josh repro with kvcache off/on, Mike runs canary with longer window, Sara wires metrics, then we meet to review. timeline OK?
Mike R.: yep. i'll file a short RFC & a perf ticket: RF-2145 (switchback selector smoothing) and assign Josh/Tanya
perf-bot: Perf alert acknowledged 2145678901. Job: small-decode-nightly. Ticket RF-2145 created. :white_check_mark:
Sara K.: small note — watch for rollout impact to small-batch-optimized customers (PLG users). hysteresis mustn't degrade steady-state win rates
Josh L.: will add test that checks steady-state throughput/latency for long-running short-seq streams
Tanya P.: if hysteresis helps but kv cache still fragments, we'll follow-up with compacting page merge strategy (coalesce nearby entries instead of evicting whole pages)
Mike R.: cool. i'll post results tomorrow morning. thanks all :thumbsup:
